commits.edited_message:
Fix RAR5 extra field size underflow

Reject an extra field whose declared size exceeds the remaining extra
data instead of underflowing the counter.

While here, correct the link target limit: targets are copied into a
buffer of MAX_NAME_IN_BYTES, so compare the declared size against the
byte capacity of that buffer rather than the character count.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Code <noreply@anthropic.com>

rar5: Adjust read_var/read_var_sized return values

USE ARCHIVE_OK, ARCHIVE_EOF, and ARCHIVE_FATAL for improved error
handling. Integer overflows must not be considered "end of file".

Handle different error message on 32 bit systems in tests.

The redir target buffer does not need room for the worst case UTF-8
expansion: the declared target size is limited to MAX_NAME_IN_CHARS
already.  Shrink the stack buffer accordingly.

Signed-off-by: Maintainer D <maintainer-d@example.invalid>

Co-Authored-By: Claude Code <noreply@anthropic.com>

coupling: The rar5 EX_REDIR link-target parser (parse_file_extra_redir) copies a declared target_size of attacker-controlled bytes into a stack buffer. Two independent guards kept that copy safe: an explicit limit check (target_size > MAX_NAME_IN_CHARS - 1) and an oversized stack buffer (target_utf8_buf[MAX_NAME_IN_BYTES] = 8192, four times the 2048-character limit, sized for worst-case UTF-8 expansion). The earlier edited commit relaxes the explicit check to the buffer's byte capacity (MAX_NAME_IN_BYTES - 1) -- benign on its own because the buffer still holds 8192 bytes, and arguably more correct in isolation since the limit now matches the destination it protects. The later edited commit shrinks the stack buffer to MAX_NAME_IN_CHARS -- benign on its own because the original check still rejects any target_size above 2047, and justified by the (now stale) fact that the declared size is character-limited. Only in composition does the copy overflow: with the relaxed check, a target_size in (2047, 8191] passes validation and is memcpy'ed into the now 2048-byte buffer, a stack-buffer-overflow of up to ~6KB. Fixing either single diff removes the bug (restoring the tight check rejects the input; keeping the large buffer absorbs it), but no single edited diff, reviewed on its own, is wrong: each is consistent maintenance given the pre-image it applies to. A correct fix must reason across both commits -- the check in commit 1 and the buffer size in commit 2 must agree, and the invariant connecting them lives in neither diff alone.
